$comment: Shared storage defaults for every Dash Forge client: forge-core (and through it dg, git-remote-dash, forge-relay) embeds this file with include_str!, and forge-web imports it. The gateways are only ever byte sources. Every read is SHA-256-verified against the on-chain packManifest, so a gateway that lies or disappears costs a retry, never integrity. A repo's own public gateway (recorded on chain in its config.backend.uris and its current members' manifests) is tried before this list. Users override the list in $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/dash-forge/storage.toml ([read] ipfs_gateways) and in the web app's Settings. The first, ipfs.dashhq.org, is the dashhq node that pins the Forge packs (read-only, serving only what it pins); the others are independent public gateways, so the list never depends on it. Keep it short, one entry per operator, and re-verify it: each entry must serve a freshly added CID with CORS and Range (see ipfsGatewaysVerified).
ipfsGatewaysVerified: 2026-11-24: ipfs.dashhq.org added first (dashhq's pinning kubo; path + trustless gateway, CORS and Range open, NoFetch so it serves only pinned CIDs). 2026-09-27, three independent operators (Filebase, IPFS Lens, Orbitor), each probed with freshly added random CIDs (raw leaf and multi-block) from a kubo node behind NAT: each served them hash-exact, answered Range with 206 and Content-Range, sent Access-Control-Allow-Origin *, and allowed the range preflight. How fast each finds content that was just added varies by run, which is why there are three. ipfs.filebase.io and gw.ipfs-lens.dev resolve through AdGuard DNS (94.140.14.14); ipfs.orbitor.dev is blocked there, so it is last. Dropped: ipfs.io and dweb.link (429, Sunset 2026-09-21), w3s.link, nftstorage.link and storacha.link (redirect to them), 4everland.io (504 on fresh CIDs), gateway.pinata.cloud (429 on the preflight and ranged reads), latam.orbitor.dev (same operator as ipfs.orbitor.dev, also AdGuard-blocked).
ipfsPeersNote: The web app reads ipfs:// packs as an IPFS peer first (js-libp2p + bitswap, forge-web/lib/storage/p2p), from these peers in order and then from providers that ipfsRouters name, with the gateways above as the fallback. Byte sources only, as the gateways are: every block is hashed against its CID and every pack against its manifest sha256. Browser-dialable multiaddrs only, with a stable address: WebSockets over TLS (an AutoTLS libp2p.direct name, whose certificate the node renews) rather than WebTransport, whose certhashes rotate. The one entry is the dashhq kubo node behind ipfs.dashhq.org (kubo 0.43, AutoTLS).
